title: Learning to sing from his mother
summary: He taught himself to sing at school and his mother helped; his sister tried piano and his mother now ushers at church.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did anybody teach you how to sing, or did you just start singing?
No, I started my own self on singing.
And how old were you when you first started singing?
I was in school, about the second grade. In fact, I used to sing a solid night without a mic every year, standing in front of all them people that had a mic every night, every Christmas Eve.
Where was that, at school?

At school, Lutheran School. But my voice was way up there, I could sing higher, I could make some higher notes there. In fact, I could sing more tenor, I could sing a lead, you know, and then I started singing a lead. But my mother actually taught me how to sing. Oh, your mother did? Yeah, my mother taught me how to sing, because she used to be how to sing. And I used to change them different types of voices, you know. That's for me, being able to do a difference between baritone and tenor, see. Well, I never could sing no bass, but I knew how it was supposed to be. But baritone and tenor, I could sing them two voices.
Well, did your mother just actually try to teach you to sing, or did you just listen to her?

I used to sing. I used to sing. See, my sister used to try to play the little piano. My sister did. And in fact, she just started off just like I did, banging, banging, banging, banging, and you look again, she was playing. Well, she don't play now. She's got too many chairs.
Well, did your mother just sing while she was around the house? Yeah. Doing work or something? Doing work, yeah. And then?
Yeah, coming behind her, getting good.
And then you'd just sing together?
Yeah, sing together like that. Yeah.
And is your mother still living? Yeah, my mother still.
Too low for me.
Huh? Oh, really?
How old is she now? Too low. My mother, she won't tell me, but I can figure from my brother's age how old she is. My mom was pretty near 80 years old.
Is she still active and gets married? Yeah. Does she still sing? No.
No. No. She's ushering in church, that's all.
She doesn't sing in church, she just goes? No, just usher.
Oh, she's in. She seats people, you know, that come in.
